visual_markers: square clay and mud-brick fort with thick sand-colored walls
four cylindrical watchtowers, one at each corner
a large central tower with a crenellated top
a small heavy wooden door set into the main gate
open paved plaza surrounding the fort in central Riyadh

facts.text_ar: حصن مبني من الطين واللبن، له أربعة أبراج مراقبة وجدران سميكة قائمة على أساس من كتل حجرية، ويقع في وسط الرياض في الأحياء القديمة.
facts.text_en: A clay and mud-brick fort with four watchtowers and thick walls founded on stone blocks, standing in the old quarter at the center of Riyadh.

facts.text_ar: بُني الحصن حوالي عام 1865 على يد عبدالرحمن بن سليمان بن دبعان، في عهد محمد بن عبدالله بن رشيد.
facts.text_en: The fort was built around 1865 by Abdulrahman ibn Sulaiman ibn Dabaan, during the rule of Mohammed ibn Abdullah ibn Rasheed.

facts.text_ar: في 14 يناير 1902 تمكّن عبدالعزيز بن عبدالرحمن آل سعود من الاستيلاء على الحصن من حامية آل رشيد، في الحدث المعروف باستعادة الرياض.
facts.text_en: On 14 January 1902 Abdulaziz bin Abdulrahman Al Saud captured the fort from its Rashid garrison, in the event known as the recapture of Riyadh.

facts.text_ar: يقع الحصن ضمن منطقة قصر الحكم، التي تضم عددًا من أبرز المعالم التراثية في الرياض.
facts.text_en: The fort sits within the Qasr Al-Hukm District, which holds several of Riyadh's most significant heritage landmarks.

visual_markers: massive free-standing red sandstone formation shaped like an elephant
a thick rock arm resembling a trunk reaching down to the ground
wide flat desert sand surrounding the base with no buildings nearby
deep horizontal erosion lines across the rock body
isolated silhouette against open sky, no vegetation

facts.text_ar: تكوين صخري طبيعي في العلا شمال غرب السعودية، يبلغ ارتفاعه 52 مترًا عند أعلى نقطة فيه.
facts.text_en: A natural rock formation in AlUla, north-western Saudi Arabia, measuring 52 metres at its highest point.

facts.text_ar: يتكوّن أساسًا من الحجر الرملي الذي تعرّض للتعرية على مدى ملايين السنين بفعل المطر والرياح والرمال حتى اتخذ شكل فيل.
facts.text_en: It is formed mainly of sandstone eroded over millions of years by rain, wind and sand until it took the shape of an elephant.

facts.text_ar: تكوّنت الصخور الرملية المحيطة بالعلا قبل نحو 540 إلى 485 مليون سنة، ثم ارتفعت قبل نحو 30 مليون سنة مع بداية انفتاح البحر الأحمر.
facts.text_en: The sandstones around AlUla formed roughly 540–485 million years ago and were uplifted about 30 million years ago as the Red Sea began to open.

facts.text_ar: يقع شرق موقع الحِجر الأثري، ويُعد أحد العجائب الجيولوجية في محافظة العلا.
facts.text_en: It lies east of the Hegra archaeological site and is considered one of AlUla Governorate's geological wonders.
Joy and fun await you in the largest entertainment center in Riyadh, Riyadh Boulevard, where endless fun destinations can be found in one place.

In addition to the luxury shopping places where you can obtain pieces from the finest stores of international brands to your closet, along with dishes that amaze your senses with flavors of local and international cuisine.
Riyadh Boulevard offers fun, joy, and enthusiasm for adults and children.
Edge of the World is the name of the 1.131 m height cliff that lies some 100 km from Riyadh at the end of the 800 km extending Tuwaik Mountain range.
Edge of the World is the perfect destination of mountain climbing and hiking lovers. Discover the breathtaking off-cliff spectacular views.
From the Earth to the moon, and from the prehistoric ages to the modern ages, the hallways of the Saudi National Museum will take you on an adventure that transcends time and space.
You will witness artistic and historical evidence in the heart of Riyadh in Al Murabba neighborhood near King Abdulaziz palace.
The museum was opened in 1419H and spans across a distance of 17,000Km2 where it tells the story of 3,700 artifacts such as statues, scripts and unique sculptures.
In the range of King Abdulaziz National Reserve, you will find the biggest natural meadow in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, with an area of ​​​​140,000 km² and extended greenery within sight.
Discover the wonderful days you will spend in Rawdat Tinhat.
One kilometer southwest of the Palace of Government, Addoho Neighborhood is located in the heart of the capital, Riyadh.
It is the last old neighborhood to preserve its traditional Najdi architecture. The construction of Addoho goes back more than 200 years.

With its strategic location within the Palace of Government area, its narrow alleys and the details of its houses that reflect the way of life of the locals at the time, Addoho Neighborhood tells the story of a desert civilization whose buildings were surrounded by walls and palm trees
The walls of Al Murabba Historial Palace are like a window to the rich history of Riyadh and a scene from its ancient memory.
The 1680 m2 of land occupied by the palace overflows with the memories of the place and the historical events it witnessed, along with the glory that was made on its land.
At a 30-km distance in the outskirts of Riyadh, on the South of the road leading to Al-Kharj, lies Heet Cave, a geological landmark about which many interesting stories have been told.
You are promised to see one of the most beautiful natural landmarks, which dates back to thousands of years.
Many exciting stories have been told about it, most notably that it was formed as a rocky cavity with a depth of 390 m inside a mountain after a celestial body struck the Earth.
Wadi Namar enables you to watch the roaming of ducks’ flocks and the spread of small fish in the Lake Dam.

Inspirational thoughts will flow to your mind as you walk along the park’s paths that extend over 2,000m, amidst the fresh air of nature, the rustle of palm trees, and the roar of the lake’s waterfalls.
The nature of the place integrates, allowing you to take pictures of the sunset or admire the starry sky at night, in a scene in which the reflected lights of the valley shine around.
The Abstract Art Gallery connects between the artist and the audience, as it hosts local art pioneers and provides a space to display their work.
Cultural and popular legacies appear on the walls of the exhibition, with their overlapping colors and artistic styles are evident in the art pieces.

The exhibition scenes allow you to immerse in plastic and abstract arts, as the pleasure increases while looking at the geometric angles and color textiles of the artworks, with the participation of a group of art connoisseurs in the exhibition.
Al Kharrarah National Park, located in the South of Al Muzahimiyah Governorate, West of Riyadh, is your spacious sanctuary to escape from the crowded city.
You can relax and sit amid nature, which is full of green landscapes, sand dunes, and a lake formed from rainfall.
Wild Sidr trees and annual plants also grow in the park. You will enjoy a serenity-filled family time.
The naturally-grassed Dirab Golf and Country Club is situated 45 km from the heart of Riyadh.
It is the first golf course with 18 holes extended over a grassy surface surrounded by amazing natural greenery and tree-lined fairways.
Escape games are amongst the most recent entertainment components in the capital, Riyadh. They are offered by Last Hour, the escape games centre, through its innovative rooms of thrilling adventures.

Naila Art Gallery provides a window to see the artistic world of beautiful paintings embodying various cultures that go beyond time and place to the colorful world of creativity and abstract art forms in the company of elite artists and critics.
You can live a unique adventure in the Escape The Room in Riyadh with your family or friends.
It includes four separate rooms, containing multiple puzzles, symbols, and codes which must be solved so that you and your group can leave the room before the specified time which is 60 minutes.
This is an adventure full of suspense and mystery, that requires mental and physical efforts, with lots of excitement and fun.
This gallery is truly an educational spot, and an artistic destination worth a visit to discover the art pieces hanging on its walls.
You will find artistic paintings that create unique styles by mixing words with drawings; it will fill you with amazement.
All of this and more is found in Riyadh, Prince Mohammed bin Saad bin Abdulaziz Road, Al Malqa.
A huge source of information and an amazing architectural masterpiece, King Fahad National Library is located on King Fahad road in Olaya district with an area of about 87,000 square meters.
Come and discover King Fahad National Library and all the exceptional content and services.
Al-Areen Equestrian Club offers many services for horse lovers including horse riding, training programs, educational programs, and horse shelter and care services in its stables.
KAFD is an iconic business and lifestyle destination with state-of-the-art physical and digital infrastructure.
An architectural marvel designed by more than 25 world-leading architectural firms, KAFD currently has 95 towers that are reshaping the skyline of Riyadh.
Al-Subaie Palace, located in Al-Shagra province in Riyadh, is one of the most significant historical palaces in Saudi Arabia.
Built in a stunning Andalusian-Islamic style, the palace sits in the southwestern corner of the Old Town, offering a magnificent view of the historic souks (markets).
This palace was once a resting place for King Abdul Aziz during his travels to and from Riyadh.
Discover the Al-Munikh Visitor Center in Al-Majma'ah, located in the southern part of the historic town.

Positioned on a strategically elevated site, this iconic watchtower provided the town's residents with unobstructed views in all directions, ensuring their safety and awareness of the surrounding areas.
A significant cultural and tourist attraction located next to Jabal Al-Nour, home of Hira Cave.
It tells the story of the divine revelation and offers insights into the historical importance of the mountain and the cave.
Hira Cultural District enriches visitors' cultural and educational experiences through its diverse facilities.

Hira Cultural District Facilities include: The Revelation Gallery Museum of the Holy Quran The way up to the cave The Cultural Library Visitor Center Commercial facilities Hira Garden and other facilities
Since the dawn of civilization, the Kaaba of Al Masjed Al Haram has had great religious significance, owing to its religious connotations associated with the Creator.

Two billion Muslims face the direction of Kaaba, to which their hearts are attached too, to perform the five daily prayers, as commanded by the Almighty, and supplicate Him for mercy, assistance and guidance.
Millions of Umrah, Hajj and prayer performers head to Makkah to perform these religious rites and enjoy the serenity of the place.
It is important to note that only Muslims may visit Al Masjed Al Haram in Makkah.

name_en: King Abdulaziz Complex for the Holy Kaaba Kiswa

facts.text_en: A specialized factory for preparing the Kiswa of the Holy Kaaba, where it is crafted from silk embroidered with gold-plated threads, forming Quranic verses that adorn the walls of the Sacred House.

Ain Zubaidah is a great archeological site of wonderful geometric design in Makkah. It reflects great care for pilgrims throughout history, as it is the oldest network used for providing pilgrims and travelers with water for 1200 years.
Masjid Al-Taneem is one of the mosques of Makkah Al-Mukarramah that is located in the western part of the city of Makkah, about 7 km away from Masjid Al-Haram.
It gained its fame because it was built in the place where Aisha bint Abu Bakr performed Umrah during the Farewell Pilgrimage in the 9th year of Hijra.

Makkah embraces many mosques that represent Islamic historical landmarks, some of them are related to a story or an event during the era of the Messenger (PBUH), and one of them is Masjid Al-Jinn near the Al-Hajun neighbourhood.
The building of the mosque is characterized by Mamluk-style architecture.

name_en: Sheikh Abdul Aziz bin Baz Mosque

facts.text_en: Sheikh Abdulaziz bin Baz Mosque is one of the largest mosques in Makkah and is famous for its distinguished location and beneficial activities.
It is one of the largest mosques in Makkah. It was established at the beginning of Ramadan in the year 1423 AH.
In the historic Al Zaher Palace, once a royal household, the Makkah Museum holds exhibits telling the history of Makkah, the archaeology of Saudi, and the story of the rise of Islam.
The building is a masterpiece of Islamic art and architecture.

The ultimate destination for astronomy enthusiasts, the museum offers an interactive and enjoyable experience for all visitors to explore the beauty of the universe, the wonders of the solar system, and the mechanisms of timekeeping.
It also offers many unique activities suitable for all age groups.
The first private museum dedicated to showcasing the history and transcription of the Holy Qur’an in Makkah, located in the Hira Cultural District.
It offers visitors a distinguished collection of rare Qur’anic manuscripts and enhances their experience with the latest museum technologies.
It presents the story of the revelation from its very first light in the Cave of Hira, along with detailed aspects of the life of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him).
The museum features halls equipped with the latest audiovisual display technologies, offering visitors an interactive experience that enriches their knowledge of the Prophet’s biography.

name_en: International Exhibition and Museum of the Biography of the Prophet and Islamic Civilization

facts.text_en: Explore the life of our Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) throughout history, his noble qualities, his Sunnah, and his life with his wives and companions.
The museum presents it in a detailed, captivating storytelling style. The exhibition is located in the King Abdulaziz Endowment - Clock Tower.

On your visit to Yanbu, you must go to Yanbu Man-Made Lake (Yanbu Lake Park). It is one of the most beautiful public places in Yanbu, where you can enjoy picturesque nature and take a walk in the open air.

The Night Market was built over 500 years ago close to the seaport in Yanbu. It was started by sailors and fishermen of the Red Sea with whatever they would bring from their fishing trips, whether treasures of the sea or trade connections.

The Market stood all these years as a historical symbol, offering its value to visitors who come all year round, decorated by unchanging originality and an archaeological spark allowing it to be one of the best tourist destinations in the West of Saudi Arabia.
Heritage monuments remain in Yanbu Historic District, which witnessed many civilizations, peoples, tribes and tumultuous historical events.
The monuments are estimated to be about 2500 years old. Yanbu Historic District is located in Yanbu Al-Bahr, south of Yanbu, on an area estimated at 45,000 square meters.
It includes about 100 heritage buildings, including mosques and various traditional markets.
An outlet for artists, Al-Sayegh House of the Arts is an exceptional destination located in the historical region of Yanbu.
It is a house with a traditional trait in its architecture inspired by the coastal nature of the city.
It includes fine arts that take you to an atmosphere full of amazement without restraining you.
On the contrary, it allows your imagination to go wild and is a tourist destination for amateur artists and art lovers.
Enjoy a relaxing picnic among the rustle of trees and the fragrances of flowers in Al Fairouz Park.
If you want to go for a walk in the fresh air, meditation nd relaxation, or if you want to have fun with your children, Al Sumayri Public Park is your destination.
Yanbu has always been a station on the trade route, and the beauty of its beaches has been attracting tourists.
Marjan Island, overlooking the enchanting blue waters of the Arabian Gulf, was opened in 1991 and the green area covers an area of up to 53,000 square meters.
The Heritage Village in Dammam is the name of the place where you can meet the past of Saudi Arabia and the heritage of its regions, on an area that extends to 21,000 square meters.
Its beautiful architecture hides within it a rich history.
The Khobar Sea Front welcomes its visitors with water and greenery, where towering trees spread as far as the eye can see and art pieces are scattered throughout.

One of the water fountains takes the shape of a shell with a shiny pearl in the middle, symbolizing one of the most beautiful treasures of the Arabian Gulf, whose crashing waves soften the atmosphere.
Sultan bin Abdulaziz Science and Technology Center (SciTech) is located on Khobar Corniche, occupying an area of 21,700 square meters.
It was established in 2000 to be a global scientific center that helps researchers, students, and enthusiasts in the fields of science and technology.
The King Abdulaziz Center for World Culture, is Saudi’s premier hub for arts, creativity, and global cultural exchange.
Located in Dhahran, this architectural masterpiece features world-class museums, interactive exhibitions, a vast library, a performing arts theater, and inspiring learning spaces.
As a leading cultural destination, Ithra hosts international events such as Japan Cultural Days, global art showcases, and thought-provoking festivals that connect Saudi with the world.
From live performances and artistic collaborations to science, literature, and history workshops, Ithra offers an immersive experience where creativity and knowledge thrive.
Enjoy Taif’s rocky terrain and its pure fresh air in Arruddaf Park. The park spans over 500m2 of land covered in nature's most vibrant colors.
You can bask in the beauty of the cirrus clouds as they float over the marvelous greenery and highlands of the park.
You can also enjoy the beautiful sounds of nature or the live musical shows accompanied by interactive water fountains.

At the top of Al-Shafa Mountain over 2500 m. above sea level, you will enjoy the natural stunning scenery of the white fog embracing the tall Sarawat Mountain peaks with its emitting aroma of juniper trees.

You can take beautiful shots of the warm sun setting down the mountains overlooking the Tohama plains, the fertile valleys, and the green fields of pomegranate, grape, and fig trees.The distance between Al-Shafa Mountains and Al-Taif is about 30 km by car through Okba Al-Mohammadia Road which connects Al-Taif to Makkah.
You must return from your trip to Taif loaded with the fragrance of roses, whether with the pictures you took to enjoy their beauty or by buying their distinguished products.
One of the most beautiful exceptional experiences that you will have is a visit to the famous factories of Taif rose products to embark on a rich and unparalleled journey of exploration.

Wahba Crater is the largest and deepest volcanic crater in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, with a diameter of 3,000 meters, and surrounded by Al Luhayan, Umm Rilan, and Zabna mountains forming a scenic view that embodies the wonders of nature in Saudi Arabia.
The Crater, which is about 380 meters deep, attracts geologists to explore its secrets and observe its diverse and exotic rock formations.
Traditional legends are known and spread among residents of nearby villages around the Crater formation.

In the historical area of ​​Taif, the exquisite architectural artistry of Al-Kaaki Palace combined juniper wood, granite stone, and colored glass to form and build the palace in the ancient Roman style, blended the spirit of the Hijaz community presented in the design of the palace windows and in the Hijazi decorations extending to the roof, forming an architectural masterpiece located on Al-Salama street.
It is time to discover the majestic Al-Hada Mountain, one of the most famous mountains in Saudi Arabia.
Al-Hada Mountain is one of Al-Sarawat Mountains range extending in a curved line of about 87 km between the two cities of Taif and Makkah.
You will certainly notice the gradual drop in temperature on your journey on Al-Hada Road.
Discover the charm of Taif's Earus Almasayif Museum, a top destination for those seeking to immerse themselves in the rich cultural and historical heritage of the region.
Wander through its beautifully curated rooms to admire fascinating artifacts, traditional crafts, and ancient architectur, all within a uniquely preserved heritage setting.

name_en: The Historical Palace of the Emirate

facts.text_en: The Aba Al-Saud neighborhood (Al-Balad) in the city of Najran embraces an important national heritage site that catches the eye of visitors immediately.

Upon arriving at the old heritage market, you will see the historic Emirate Palace in all its splendor and grandeur, providing an idea of the architectural fabric of the mud houses in Najran, and serving as an inspiring cultural framework for visitors and tourists, and a bridge of communication between generations.
The historic city of Al-Okhdood is located southwest of Najran, with a past that dates back to ancient times.
It witnessed periods of history that extend to 1000 BC, and its history reveals human civilizations over different historical periods.
King Fahd Park is located in the Saqam Forest and is one of the most important natural recreational landmarks in the city and its largest park.
The park is characterized by its stunning natural scenery and breathtaking views, and it offers a range of enjoyable activities suitable for all family members.
Najran is adorned with many majestic palaces that have formed a historical legacy for the region, including the historic Al-Aan Palace, also known as Saadan Palace.

The palace is located on Al-Aan Mountain, from which it takes its name. It was built in 1100 AH (1689/1688 CE), and has undergone several renovations, the latest of which was in 1440 AH (2019/2018 CE).

Najran Regional Museum allows visitors to take a walk through history, showcasing important glimpses of the region that formed Najran through various inscriptions from civilizations dating back to prehistoric times, as well as documentary photographs of the caravan route.

Al Manjam Palace is located in Najran, specifically in the village of Al Manjam. This ancient building takes its visitors on a heritage journey through time, going back to the year 1688 when it was built.
It passes through important historical stages that tell the story of the region, its heritage, and its glory.
Al Hamra Park in Al Jubail is a recreational area for the residents of the neighborhood, covering an area of 75,000 square meters.

It includes chairs distributed throughout its extent, a pedestrian path, a bicycle path, as well as a football field and a play area for children, allowing the whole family to enjoy special times amidst greenery and fresh air.
Crease Tower is a mud tower that tells the story of glory preserved in the memory of history.

It is located in the western part of Al Jubail in the Eastern Region of Saudi Arabia. It was built by order of the founder King Abdulaziz bin Abdulrahman Al Saud in 1928, coinciding with the period of the emergence of the city of Al Jubail at that time.
The tower is considered a historical legacy and an important landmark in the region, visited by tourists, antiquities enthusiasts, and history lovers.

Dareen Hills Park in Al Jubail is characterized by its pleasant atmosphere, refreshing breeze, and stunning nature, covered with vast green spaces overlooking the seaside, making it an ideal daily destination.

With its view of the Arabian Gulf coast, Al Nakheel Corniche in Al Jubail is a wonderful tourist destination for beach lovers and walking on the sand, where you can face the successive waves of the sea and enjoy quiet moments in its seating areas designed in the form of a traditional "arish" structure.

You will not only see the Aseer legacies in Alraqdi Museum, but it will also open the doors of knowledge that will take you to ancient worlds and historical anecdotes that express the history of ancient Aseer, adorned with the arts of Al-Qatt Al-Aseer made by Aseer women.
In an astonishing experience, Art Street takes you on a trip full of colors and creativity to another dimension in the arts space, to taste the works of artists and creators of the region.
Immerse yourself in an exceptional journey out of the ordinary and prepare to discover one of the most beautiful art streets in the world.
Step into the Al-Qatt Al-Aseeri Museum, where the vibrant and intricate art of Al-Qatt Al-Aseeri comes to life.
This unique museum, dedicated to the traditional art and heritage of Aseer’s women, offers an immersive experience that showcases their distinctive style in home decoration and daily life.
From the moment you enter, the aromatic plants at the entrance welcome you into a world of colorful geometric patterns and lively decorations.
The walls adorned with Al-Qatt's vibrant lines and shapes tell stories of cultural heritage and artistic expression, recognized by UNESCO as an intangible cultural heritage.
Embark on a timeless journey to Rijal Heritage Village, a gem just 45 km from Abha. This stunning village, with its vibrant stone buildings and unique architecture, showcases 700 years of history.
Recognized globally as one of the best tourist villages, Rijal is a treasure trove of cultural tales and rare exhibits.

Al-Mushait Palaces are located in the South of Khamis Mushait. Their square shape and the materials used for their construction showcase the expertise of the people of the region and their way of benefitting from their virgin nature.
That is because it is the most capable of enduring the weather and due to their abundance at the time.
Discover the charm of The Vineyard, a picturesque farm where you can wander through lush fields brimming with a variety of local fruits.
Located in the heart of Aseer, this farm offers a delightful escape into nature, featuring figs, grapes, pomegranates, and peaches.
Enjoy a leisurely stroll through the orchards, where the vibrant colors and fresh scents of the fruits create an enchanting atmosphere.
The Vineyard also provides comfortable seating areas where you can relax and savor delicious meals and refreshing drinks surrounded by stunning natural beauty.
Step into Zabna Historic Village, where the echoes of a rich past meet the serenity of nature.
This unique destination invites you to explore beautifully restored ancient houses and a heritage mosque, each structure telling the story of the region's storied history.
As you wander through the village, you'll feel the charm of traditional architecture and the warmth of a community that has preserved its cultural legacy through the centuries.
The peaceful environment offers a perfect retreat for heritage enthusiasts and nature lovers alike, providing a unique glimpse into the timeless beauty of Aseer.
Perched atop the highest peaks of Manaa, Mountain Cottage offers a unique retreat for those seeking tranquility and breathtaking views.
This rustic haven, situated in the heart of Tanomah, immerses you in the serene beauty of mountain life, far from the hustle and bustle of daily life.
Mountain Cottage is designed with an innovative blend of recycled materials, including aged wood and dried trees, creating a cozy and sustainable interior.
Relax in the fresh mountain air and let the soothing sounds of nature transport you to a world of peace and serenity.
Step into the Heritage Civilization Palace Museum (Al Maqar), a breathtaking architectural marvel that seamlessly blends Andalusian and Islamic designs.
Located in the heart of Aseer, this palace is adorned with intricate Islamic decorations and houses, a vast collection of ancient manuscripts and artifacts.
Explore the palace's extensive collection, including over a thousand handwritten Quranic manuscripts, making it the foremost repository of such treasures.
The museum's rich history is complemented by its luxurious accommodations and diverse guest services, ensuring a memorable visit.
For breakfast enthusiasts seeking a modern twist on traditional flavors, Areesh is your go-to destination.

This cozy spot reinvents the Saudi breakfast experience with a contemporary flair, offering a diverse array of dishes that preserve the essence of traditional recipes while adding a fresh, modern touch.
The ambiance, infused with the warmth of home and distinctive heritage decor, creates a perfect setting for couples looking to start their day with a unique and satisfying meal.
From freshly baked bread to innovative takes on classic dishes, each bite at Areesh tells a story of culinary tradition meeting modern creativity.
Nestled within the lush expanse of Tabab Heights, Cypress Cottage offers a unique blend of modern comfort and rural charm.

This thoughtfully designed retreat, inspired by European countryside lodges, provides an unforgettable stay amidst more than a hundred towering cypress trees, making it an ideal escape for nature enthusiasts.
At Cypress Cottage, you'll find yourself surrounded by breathtaking greenery and refreshingly cool temperatures, a hallmark of the Tabab region.
The cottage itself boasts contemporary furniture crafted from ancient trees, some over a thousand years old, seamlessly blending rustic aesthetics with modern amenities.
Experience the awe-inspiring beauty of Alsamaa Eaqabat View, a breathtaking vantage point in the Aseer region that offers unparalleled views of the surrounding mountains and valleys.
This scenic spot, a vital link between the peaks of Al Soudah and the villages of Al Sharaf and Rabia, leads you down to the historic province of Rijal Almaa.
At Alsamaa Eaqabat View, you can immerse yourself in the stunning landscape that unfolds before you.
The panoramic vistas are particularly captivating at sunset, when the sky is painted with hues of orange and pink.
Enjoy the charming sunset with a view of the surrounding countryside, forests, mountains, and fog.
Immerse yourself in the breathtaking natural beauty of Al Habala Park, a stunning attraction in the Aseer region that promises an unforgettable experience for all visitors.
Located at a high altitude, this park offers panoramic views where the sky seamlessly merges with the earth, creating a serene and picturesque setting.
At Al Habala Park, you can enjoy a variety of activities that cater to all family members.
Take a thrilling ride on the cable car, which provides spectacular aerial views of the surrounding landscape.
Nestled in the picturesque village of Rijal Almaa, Honey Cottage offers an enchanting escape into the heart of nature.

This rustic retreat, crowned with a charming windmill, provides not only stunning views of the surrounding landscape but also a delightful array of locally produced honey, making it a honey lover's paradise.
At Honey Cottage, you can immerse yourself in the serene beauty of the Aseer region. The cottage is designed in a traditional wooden style, surrounded by lush greenery and natural valleys.
Here, you can taste over 40 different types of honey, each with its unique flavor profile, harvested from the local flora.
Liwan Farm offers a unique rural retreat where visitors can experience the charm and simplicity of farm life.
Nestled amidst beautiful landscapes, the farm provides a serene environment perfect for families and nature lovers looking to escape the hustle and bustle of city life and reconnect with nature.
Enjoy a stay at the authentic inn and explore a variety of cafes and restaurants catering to all tastes.
The farm also reflects Aseer’s rich history, showcased in a museum with unique and rare artifacts.
Al Basta District is one of the oldest residential areas in Abha, featuring historical buildings and ancient architecture.
It is renowned for its traditional old town market with various vendors serving street food, concept stores, and souvenir shops.
The district's open square creates a lively social atmosphere perfect for spending quality time with family and friends.
Don't miss the chance to learn about the stories of the Aseer community up close.
Explore Almuftaha Village in Abha, known for its traditional mud buildings and rich Aseer heritage.
The village features the King Fahd Cultural Center, Almuftaha Palace Museum, and numerous shops selling honey, antiques, and local delicacies, all within a charming traditional setting.
Throughout different seasons, the village comes alive with various events, enhancing its vibrant cultural atmosphere.
Step into Clouds, a hotel and residential retreat where modern elegance blends with Aseer tradition.
Enjoy the breathtaking views at Juliette Restaurant and Café, where every meal is a feast for the senses.
Unwind in our luxurious spa and experience the perfect blend of comfort and style at Clouds.

name_en: Preserved tombs and ancient wonders at Hegra

facts.text_en: Saudi Arabia's first UNESCO World Heritage Site, Hegra reveals the fascinating Nabataean history with over 110 preserved tombs and ancient wonders.
It offers a captivating glimpse into AlUla's rich heritage, making it an essential destination for anyone exploring AlUla.
Embark on an exciting celestial adventure far out in the desert on a stargazing trip to Gharameel.
Hear from an expert guide as you admire the blanket of stars overhead while surrounded by photogenic pillars of mountain rock that reach skywards.
Embark on a historic journey in AlUla and uncover the ancient sites of Dadan and Jabal Ikmah.
These two heritage sites are significant archaeological marvels that captivate the world even now.

Step into the realm of Maraya, an architectural marvel in AlUla's Ashar Valley. This mirrored wonder, blending into the sandstone cliffs, offers a surreal experience as it appears and disappears with your every step.
A crossroads of civilisations and oasis city on incense-trading routes, people have inhabited AlUla for thousands of years.
By preserving its rich heritage and continuing to flourish as a rural tourist destination, it has been awarded Best Tourism Village by the United Nations World Tourism Organization.
Today, AlUla Old Town Village encompasses its ancient Old Town, the lush Oasis and the AlJadidah Arts District.
Translating to “Valley of the Arts,” this new cultural destination is a blank canvas for large-scale art.
Take a walking tour through the valley to see some unique, dramatic, and impressive works of contemporary art.
Experience the thrill of AlUla’s Giant Swing—a breathtaking adventure that lets you soar 85 meters above the ground, gliding through a 70-meter arc over stunning desert landscapes.
Perched atop a mountain, this unique experience is perfect for thrill-seekers ready to test their limits and embrace the excitement of swinging high above the mesmerizing terrain of AlUla.
Feel the adrenaline rush as you enjoy unparalleled views and an unforgettable journey in one of Saudi's most scenic locations.
In the midst of AlUla’s golden desert sands, the lush date palm groves of AlUla Oasis thrive as a vibrant symbol of life and sustainability.
Producing over 90,000 tonnes of dates each year, this oasis has supported the region's ecosystem and economy for centuries.

Merchants, pilgrims, and travelers journeying to ancient sites like Dadan and Hegra found refuge under its shaded groves, using its wood for shelter and fuel, while local communities flourished from its bounty.

Today, AlUla Oasis invites visitors to explore its rich natural and cultural heritage through guided tours, unique dining experiences amid the palm groves, and a variety of activities that showcase the oasis's enduring legacy.
Embark on a mesmerizing journey with AlUla’s hot air balloon experience, lifting you 1,200 meters above the ground for panoramic views of the region’s majestic desert landscapes and ancient sites.
Float gently above sandstone mountains, verdant oases, and historic landmarks like Hegra, capturing the beauty of AlUla from a vantage point like no other.
Whether it’s the golden hues at sunrise or the dramatic colors of sunset, this hot air balloon ride promises an unforgettable adventure and a unique way to explore the awe-inspiring scenery of Saudi.
Embark on an unforgettable adventure with the AlUla Stairway—a 45-meter suspended stairway offering breathtaking views and an adrenaline-pumping climb.
After reaching the summit, feel the thrill as you zipline back down into the valley, completing an experience that perfectly combines excitement with the stunning landscapes of AlUla.
Ideal for adventure seekers, the AlUla Stairway promises a unique way to explore the rugged beauty of this historic region.
A peaceful and entertaining atmosphere awaits you at Juman Park, located in King Abdullah Economic City, adjacent to the canal Bay La Sun district, specifically between Bay La Sun Hotel and Marina.
The park has a total area of about 55,000 square meters and features beautifully designed green spaces overlooking the stunning blue canal.
It provides a refreshing and joyful experience for your soul and includes facilities and activities that will create lasting memories for you and your family.
Do you love golf? Or perhaps you want to test your skills in this fascinating global sport through a miniature experience?
Maybe your children have shown interest in playing golf? If so, you're in for a treat with the Juman Mini Golf course, located in the unique Juman Park of King Abdullah Economic City (KAEC).
Karting is a type of high-speed car racing that is popular all over the world.
Located on the north side of King Abdul Aziz International Airport, King Abdullah Sports City has various stadiums and is just 19 minutes away from Jeddah Corniche Circuit.

It is considered the second sports destination in Jeddah full of excitement and enthusiasm, and only two minutes away from "Jeddah Superdome," a wonderful opportunity to attend more than one event in a day.

King Abdullah Sports City hosted the most prominent international sports events, attracting many sports and thousands of fans interested in these extraordinary events, such as The first “WWE” Freestyle Wrestling Championship and Dakar Rally in 2021.
Here is where unparalleled adventures and many world concerts were held, which made it one of the most important entertainment destinations in Saudi Arabia.

Jeddah has a history that predates modern Arabia. As one of the Gulf’s oldest seaports and the gateway to the holy city of Makkah, Jeddah has been welcoming the world for centuries — which has helped transform the city into the culturally rich melting pot it is today.
For a fascinating look into Jeddah’s long and cosmopolitan past, take a trip to the Tayebat Museum for a superbly curated representation of the city’s 2,500-year history.

Located in the Al Faisaliyah district, the museum is housed in a multiroom complex that re-creates the traditional Hijazi architecture of the old city, with bay windows overlaid with intricate wooden lattice work and ornate coral masonry.
With several floors of in-depth exhibits, the museum offers a living history lesson on the foundation of Jeddah, Saudi Arabia and the wider Arabian Peninsula.

Located just off Al Kurnaysh Road on Jeddah’s north corniche, Fakieh Aquarium is the first marine exhibition of its kind in Saudi Arabia, and it’s no coincidence that it finds itself within earshot of the city’s lapping Red Sea.
The sprawling tunnels and vast tanks that make up the aquarium house over 200 species and around 85 percent of them are native to Jeddah’s undisturbed coral reefs.
It makes this colorful window onto the Red Sea the best way to experience the region’s vibrant underwater ecosystem without needing to squeeze into scuba gear.

Accompanied by a meditative soundtrack and enclosed in cavern walls, a trip through the aquarium brings you face-to-face with some of the 800 Red Sea oddities that don’t exist anywhere else on the planet.
Visible from all across the city, King Fahd Fountain is a much-loved Jeddah landmark and a 30-year-old monument in the middle of the Red Sea.

At 312 meters high, its waters decorate the sunset of Jeddah, and whether you are thinking of taking a picture or a video of that magical scene, seeing the fountain will not seem impossible no matter how far away you are.
As the spectacular display of the fountain continues, you can walk around and try different kinds of food along the various stalls in Alhamra Cornish.
Seven is the most popular kiosk on the walkway.
Before naming it as the royal seaport for Makkah at 657 AD, the Al-Balad site, “Historic Jeddah”, was built on beautiful coastal land.

It gathered people from all cultures and walks of life throughout the ages. This part of the world unveils a human heritage whose walls challenged different historical factors with eight gates; each is known for its historical stories.
In addition, it holds more than 10 ancient houses praised for their distinctive designs and the names of their ancient families.
Here, you will get the coziest photographs.
Even in the octane-fueled world of Formula One racing, known for its powerfully muscled hot rods, the Jeddah Corniche Circuit is breaking speed records.

The track, situated along Saudi’s Red Sea coastline, is “the fastest street circuit ever seen in Formula One,” according to the Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile, the governing body for motorsports.
It also boasts the most corners: 27.
This is no doubt the place everybody adores, a place that instantly and seamlessly delights and revitalizes your heart.
It is precisely where visitors fall deeply captive in Jeddah. Strap on your shoes and come explore one of the latest waterfronts in the world.
Tariq Abdulhakim Center Museum showcases the journey of one of Saudi’s most influential and pioneering musicians, and the first Arab musician to receive the UNESCO World Prize.
Visitors can enjoy his distinctive compositions and melodies, and view his musical instruments, belongings, and notes to gain insight into his artistic environment and illustrious career.
Obhur Corniche is one of Jeddah's premier waterfront destinations, perfect for strolling and spending quality time with family and friends.
Enjoy the breathtaking views of the Red Sea while taking advantage of its diverse recreational facilities, making it an ideal spot for everyone.
teamLab Borderless opened its doors for the first time in the Middle East in Jeddah! a collection of artworks that form one continuous, borderless world.
These artworks move freely out of the rooms, creating connections and relationships with people, communicating with other works, and sometimes intermingling with each other.
They share the same concept of time as the human body, creating a unique and immersive experience.
Borderless World Visitors wander through this borderless world, exploring with intention, creating and discovering new experiences with others.
Discover the innovative spirit of Hayy Jameel, featuring a wide range of seasonal art shows, workshops, and cultural festivities.
Spend a day with your family exploring the vibrant art scene and creative community of Jeddah.

Spanning across both distance and time, the Hejaz Railway was established at the beginning of the twentieth century to connect Damascus and Madina in a journey that took no more than five days, compared to the previous 45 days that were required, which involved crossing barren deserts and rugged terrain.

Tabuk Province is rich with numerous archaeological sites that reveal the history of the area, allowing us to witness symbols of an ancient past, such as Tabuk Archaeological Castle, which dates back over five centuries and is now one of the most important historical castles and tourist landmarks in the region.

On a sunny day or a cold night in Tabuk, you can lay on the green grass that stretches over an area of 500,000 square meters in Prince Fahad Bin Sultan Park, families and friends gather while enjoying a cup of Saudi coffee flavoured with saffron and cardamom, surrounded by lush trees and fresh air.

A collection of facilities that contain items that date back to Tabuk's rich past can be found in Tabuk Attraction Mud House, or as it is commonly known, the Mud House Museum, which houses various archaeological details and is one of the most prominent tourist landmarks in Tabuk.
The nature in Tabuk City is diverse and includes many green spaces, including gardens equipped with all services, numbering about 44 gardens, including Al Murooj Park.
Al-Tawbah Mosque in Tabuk represents an important Islamic landmark as the site where it was built is connected to events from the Battle of Tabuk.
The mosque serves as a vital point in the region, around which the markets and neighbourhoods of Tabuk are clustered.
It is a majestic mountain that had a special place to the Prophet, blessings and peace be upon him, who said: "Uhud is a mountain that loves us and we love it."

It is the first mosque in Islam. The Prophet, blessings and peace be upon him, with his own blessed hands, laid the foundation stone of the mosque, which was built by the emigrants and the helpers (ansar).
Allah extolled this mosque and mentioned its virtues in the everlasting Qur'an, "A mosque founded on righteousness from the first day is more worthy for you to stand in." (9:108)
Today, it is 200 meters away from the courtyards of the Prophet’s Mosque. It was one of the Prophet's prayer grounds, to which he would go out to lead people in Eid and rain-invoking prayers.
It embraces memories of the Prophet's life and the fragrant civilizational history of Muslims.

It is one of the most important historical mosques in Madinah. In this mosque, Allah honored the Prophet, blessings and peace be upon him, and fulfilled his wish by shifting the qiblah direction from Jerusalem to the Kaaba: (We will surely turn you to a qiblah with which you will be pleased) [Qur'an 2:144].
The Palace is an emblem of defiance and steadfastness in the face of the forces of nature.
It was built on a high hill overlooking the edges of Al-Aqiq Valley in the west of Madinah.

Uhud Martyrs Square is one of the most famous landmarks that Muslims are keen to visit because it represents a historical memory associated with the events of the Battle of Uhud, which took place in the third year of the Prophet’s emigration.
It is one of the most important historical landmarks of Madinah. On their way to the Sacred Mosque of Makkah, pilgrims from or passing through Madinah stop at this mosque.
Here they give up all worldly appearances and put on Ihram garments in their journey of faith, hoping only for Allah's mercy and reward in the Hereafter.
The museum is considered one of the historical tourist destinations in Madinah. It was established in 1419 AH, corresponding to 1998 AD, and was inaugurated by Prince Abdulmajeed ibn Abdulaziz.
It is located on Omar ibn Al-Khattab St, King Abdulaziz Square in Anbariya. It is about 1,020 meters away from the Prophet’s Mosque.

Madinah’s most famous castle was built for surveillance and protection. Made from thick, black volcanic stones and covered with white plaster, the castle is located about 1,500 meters from Quba Mosque on a high hill in the Al Duwaima neighborhood.
Located in the area of the Seven Mosques, Ali ibn Abi Talib Mosque is a destination for visitors who want to explore Islamic cultural heritage.
The Prophet Muhammad performed Eid prayer on the site, as did Ali ibn Abi Talib after the Prophet's death.
A destination that reflects the history and culture of Medina, featuring many local and cultural experiences.
Explore the second-holiest city in Islam on top of our comfortable double-decker buses to discover its rich Islamic history, heritage, culture, and social life.
A special Ramadan market containing 60 outlets for owners of local products will be activated during the month of Ramadan to sell Ramadan products and food.

A cultural tourist oasis, in which the visitor moves between Many diverse items, the most prominent of which is the museum The story of creation, the cultural park and waterways as well as areas of shops, restaurants and cafes.
Alsirah offers an immersive experience that sheds light on the life, journey, and lessons of the prophet Mohammad (PBUH).
By narrating inspiring stories from his profound journey, our experiences foster a deeper connection to him and a greater appreciation for his legacy.
Souq Suwaiqah is one of the oldest and most prominent markets in Madinah. It is characterized by traditional products that Reflect the authenticity of Saudi crafts and their ancient history.
By selling and reviewing invasive products, it collects the market between ancient and modern sculpting works and supports women's empowerment by involving them in the Sale and crafts.

The heritage district is located within King Fahd Central Park, The project aims to launch a cultural festival throughout the month of Ramadan that combines cultural and entertainment experiences and events.
In addition to restaurants and cafes serving all local cuisine.
The Ayer View offers a unique Madani Ramadan Iftar experience with a stunning panoramic view of Madinah.

name_en: The International Fairs and Museums of the Prophet’s Biography and Islamic Civilization

facts.text_en: The exhibition showcases the Prophet’s biography with interactive displays in seven languages.

Jawatha is located in the northeast of Al Hofuf, and it is a tourist city that was opened in 2018 to be a distinctive destination that includes historical monuments, popular markets, and enjoyable activities.
It welcomes visitors daily from 8:00 am to midnight.

name_en: Largest Palm Oasis in the World

facts.text_en: The natural oasis of Al-Ahsa, whose area exceeds 85 square kilometers, reveals geographical artifacts that are full of details of its unique terrain and the diversity of its environment, including caves, mountains, plains, and springs, to be deservedly included in the UNESCO World Heritage List since 2018.

Al Asfar Lake appears amidst the golden dunes and in a charming scene, which was formed by seasonal rain over decades and is locally called (the summer blue and the winter white) because its color changes according to seasons.

It is one of the largest natural water bodies in the Gulf region and has been transformed into a nature reserve to encompass the surrounding wildlife, as desert plants surround the lake, trees converge around it and cover the horizon, the soft and pure sands remain.

Step into Bayt Al-Bay'ah in Al-Ahsa, a historic landmark built in 1203 AH (1788 CE) by Sheikh Abdul Rahman Al-Mulla, capturing the elegance of traditional Saudi architecture during the First Saudi State.
Located in the Al-Rawda neighborhood of Al-Kut, this house is where the people of Al-Ahsa pledged loyalty to King Abdulaziz Al Saud on the night of Jumada Al-Akhirah 5, 1331 AH (1912 CE).
Owned at the time by Sheikh Abdul Latif Al-Mulla, Mufti of Al-Ahsa, the house holds the very room where King Abdulaziz rested.
Today, Bayt Al-Bay'ah invites history enthusiasts and culture lovers to explore its charm.
Al Ahsa Governorate has an enormous historical inventory that dates back centuries BC. The human civilizations followed one another in Al Ahsa.

Being a natural oasis in an ideal location made Al-Ahsa desired by many. However, its people worked to protect it from enemies by building castles and palaces with towers that gave them a comprehensive view of their surroundings.
One of the most important protective palaces in Al Ahsa is Sahoud Palace.
Handcraft Castle is one of the most important landmarks in Al-Ahsa, with its traditional heritage character.
This is why it was included in the Creative Cities Network of UNESCO in the craft and folk-art creative field.

Al-Ahsa is home to many historic mosques that still preserve their mud structure adorned with unique architectural designs as if they were an open book that tells the story of historical eras that have passed.
Among the historic treasures that have stood the test of time is Masjid Al-Jalaniah, dating back to the 12th century AD, surrounded by towering palm forests near water springs.
Explore Qasr Ibrahim, a historic landmark at the center of Al-Hofuf’s Al-Kut neighborhood.

Covering 18,200 square meters, this palace—built during the Al-Jabri dynasty (1436–1534 CE) and also known as "Qasr Al-Qubba" or "Qasr Al-Kut"—represents Al-Hofuf’s past as a thriving trade hub and fortress of power.
Enjoy its blend of religious and military architecture: from the iconic Islamic domes, arches, and mosque mihrab to the towering walls, soldier barracks, and stables that reveal its defensive legacy.
Discover the captivating caves of Al Qarah Mountain, shaped over centuries by natural processes like the dissolving of water-soluble rocks, abrasion, and earthquake fissures.
These unique formations boast 28 tall linear passageways stretching 1.5 kilometers, offering a maze of wonder for explorers and history enthusiasts alike.
Among the most famous caves are Al Nashab, known for its moderate temperatures year-round, and Bu Saleh, Al Eid, An Naqa, Al Mua'adhamah, and Al Maheub, each holding its own charm and stories.
Some caves even host workshops for local potters, adding a cultural touch to the experience.
Raghadan Forest Park in Al Baha stands out as one of the largest and most celebrated forests in Saudi, covering an extensive area often shrouded in fog.

Perched at a high elevation, it is home to trees that have stood for centuries. Raghadan Forest Park is a hub of activities, events, and facilities for all ages, featuring stunning views of Al Baha's natural scenery, foggy peaks, waterfalls, a suspension bridge elevated 13 to 15 meters, and exciting zipline adventures.
The park also includes a children's play area, shopping, and dining options, providing visitors with an opportunity to immerse themselves in nature and various exciting activities.

Thee Ain Historical Village is located in Al-Makhwah Governorate in Al Baha, on the top of a rugged white mountain overlooking Wadi Rash from the western side, while being surrounded by mountain heights.
Thee Ain is about 25 km far from the center of Al-Baha city and is considered one of the most important heritage villages in the Arabian Peninsula.

Seeing it from the outside, the village may appear as a single castle. Dating back to the tenth century AH, the village gained its name from a spring that passes through it, pouring from the surrounding mountains.
The village includes a small mosque and more than 30 houses, all of which are designed to be contiguous and superimposed on each other due to the village's mountainous nature.

Al-Zaytouna Farm in Al-Baha spans an area of approximately 150,000 square meters, with one hundred agricultural terraces extending along the Sarawat Mountains, specifically in Bahar Center on the Al-Aqiq road.

The farm includes more than 4,000 olive trees, in addition to three tanks for storing rainwater, a bird breeding garden, and a horse stud, making it a stunning destination for tourists all year round, offering a charming experience in picking agricultural crops, enjoying scenic views, and savoring delicious dishes prepared on-site by skilled chefs.
On the slope of a towering hill in the village of Bani Saar, north of Al-Baha city, lies the historical Palace of Bin Raqoush.
Its construction dates back to 1834 and it was considered a complete residential system consisting of several family homes and guesthouses headed by the "Zahran" council.

name_en: Regional Museum of Antiquities and Heritage

facts.text_en: The earlier inhabitants left behind evidence and traces that tell something about their lives and narrate a summary of their stories.
You can explore these stories as you wander through the Regional Museum of Antiquities and Heritage in Al-Baha.
The museum has collected historical pieces that silently recount the region's stories and ancient shapes and inscriptions that captivate visitors' imaginations.
Al Malad Castle, aka Twin Fortresses, is a prominent feature of the heritage of Al-Baha Province.
It is a twin fortress located in the historic village of Al Malad, atop a hill that lies on the commercial road leading to Aseer.
A'arif Fort stands out with its ancient details and reflects the rich cultural history of the city of Hail.
It was built in 1840, and it was named after the mountain on which it was built.
Aja Park in Hail has many facilities that are suitable for all members of the family. You will find chalets, and the largest open space games area in Hail awaits you.
There are also places to ride horses, a shopping area, and various restaurants and cafes.

Historians describe Faid Historic City as the third most important ancient city after Kufa and Basra, as it was located along the ancient Iraqi pilgrimage route known as Zubaida Trail, which connected Iraq with Makkah.
The city is located in southeast Hail, 120 km away from it.

Al Mutlaq Heritage Mosque has been the subject of the Mutlaq family's care for more than three centuries, passing down the responsibility of its maintenance and restoration from generation to generation.
It is one of the oldest and most prominent historical mosques in northern Saudi Arabia, with its foundations rooted in the city of Hail.
Discover Barzan Palace in the heart of Hail, a historic landmark and one of the region's most important urban heritage sites.
Built with towering architecture that once rose above the city’s buildings, Barzan Palace’s two remaining towers—one to the north and another to the south—reach approximately 12 meters high.

Named "Barzan" because it stood prominent among the city’s structures, the palace is now a celebrated tourist attraction, inviting visitors to experience its architectural legacy and significance within Hail's heritage landscape.
Discover Al-Qashla Castle in Hail, an iconic heritage site that showcases the traditional Najdi architectural style.
Built during the reign of King Abdul Aziz in 1360 AH (1941 CE), Al-Qashla stands as a symbol of Hail’s rich urban heritage.
Constructed from clay and stones, the castle features intricate plaster decorations with geometric and floral motifs typical of traditional architecture in the region.
Its 12-meter-high cylindrical defensive towers, including four internal "Al-Sandah" towers, emphasize its defensive strength.
Journey through time at Umm Sinman, a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2015, and one of Saudi's most prominent rock art locations.

Situated in the northern region of the Kingdom, the rock faces of Mount Umm Sinman are adorned with human and animal carvings from various historical eras, with the oldest dating back over 12,000 years to the beginning of the Neolithic era.
The site also includes ancient Thamudian inscriptions and early Islamic writings, with some inscriptions dating back to 147 AH.
These remarkable carvings offer a glimpse into the cultural richness and deep history of human settlement in Jubbah, capturing the essence of ancient life across millennia.

Discover Turan Village, located 55 kilometers from Hail. Known as the land of the legendary Arab figure Hatim Al-Ta’i, Turan celebrates the enduring legacy of his unmatched generosity, immortalized in Arab culture with the phrase, "More generous than Hatim." Today, the village preserves remnants of its storied past, including a fortress near the entrance believed to have been Hatim's palace.

In the village center, visitors can explore the ruins of an ancient mud palace and a small cemetery with two unusually long graves—one of which, stretching 9.5 meters, is believed by locals to be the resting place of Hatim Al-Ta’i, while the other is thought to belong to his daughter, who is said to have witnessed the dawn of Islam.

Visit Al Adham, nestled amidst stunning mountains and a uniquely serene landscape, immerse yourself in the enchanting "Qumra" event, a celebration of Saudi heritage with captivating Samri performances.
Held for three nights each Hijri month (14th, 15th, and 16th, excluding Ramadan), this event fills the air with traditional melodies in a vibrant setting under the refreshing evening breeze.
Don't miss the spectacular horse shows featuring skilled riders, both men and women, showcasing their artistry and mastery.
These breathtaking displays take place during the first three days of each Gregorian month.
Discover Al Samra Mountain, a part of the Shammar Mountains located east of Hail, steeped in history and captivating tales.
History reveals that Hatim Al-Tai lit a fire on its summit, known as "Al Mawqida," to guide travelers and passersby to his home.
Today, Al Samra Mountain features breathtaking views, a scenic overlook, and an Italian restaurant and cafe offering a unique dining experience.
Whether you're exploring its historic legacy or enjoying its serene atmosphere, Al Samra Mountain is a destination that beautifully blends heritage and modern leisure.
You cannot learn the history of a region without visiting its museums and historical sites, as museums represent a wonderful means of showcasing heritage and transferring it to future generations.
During your visit to the Qassim region, you may find a great opportunity to learn about the region's heritage and culture by visiting the Al-Oqilat Museum.
King Khalid Park in Buraidah is a destination for relaxation. Its lush green spaces and shady trees are in a vast area designed to accommodate family and friend gatherings.
It offers a joyful outdoor atmosphere and the beauty of nature.
A tourist landmark where visitors can learn about the cultural, social, and industrial heritage of the region.
The fragrant smell of perfumes fills the alleys of the historic Mithnab Village, introducing visitors to the authentic heritage of Qassim Province.
The village clings to its extreme authenticity, as the traditional mud houses welcome you with their ancient construction and lanterns hanging on their walls.
The old inhabitants of the province narrate the history of Qassim, as their memories are filled with stories and tales that they preserve with utmost care.
The Shamasiyah Museum is one of the important landmarks in the Shamasiyah governorate, Al-Qassim Province.
It displays a diverse collection of rare historical artifacts and introduces important personalities from the region's intellectuals, thinkers, and leaders.
Explore Al Bassam Heritage House, a remarkable example of Najdi architecture located near the western gate of Unayzah city.

Constructed between 1374 and 1378 AH, this 3,500-square-meter house showcases the architectural ingenuity of Najd with its intricate designs, stone foundations, and tamarisk wood features, including ceilings, doors, and windows.
The house consists of four distinct sections: the men’s reception area, a family section, a garden, and animal pens.
Visitors can also explore the majlis, an open yard, and a dining hall, each space echoing the region’s cultural and architectural heritage.
Enjoy your time in a distinctive destination that combines authenticity with the serene charm of a wintry atmosphere.

The promenade winds through historic palm farms with over 700 palm trees, some of which are more than 100 years old, showcasing the agricultural heritage of the region in a setting that offers tranquillity and a connection to nature.
It’s the perfect spot for a stroll among the palms or a relaxing meal at one of the many restaurants and cafes, offering diverse options to suit all tastes.

The Palms Avenue isn’t just a place to visit; it’s a moment to pause, reflect, and enjoy the seamless blend of heritage and nature, making it a favourite for families and seekers of unique experiences.
Maqsourat Al-Rajhi is a stunning collection of mud houses located amid palm plantations in the southeastern part of Bukayriyah province.
Built over 250 years ago by Sheikh Nasser Al-Rajhi, this historical site exemplifies the craftsmanship of Najdi architecture.
The site includes a traditional mosque and an ancient well, where the historic Swani irrigation method was used to draw water.
Recently restored to closely resemble its original form, Maqsourat Al-Rajhi served as a welcoming haven for travelers and guests.
Maqsourat Al-Swailim is one of the most iconic heritage landmarks in Bukayriyah, blending the charm of the past with modern refinement.

Built by the former Prince of Bukayriyah, Abdullah bin Swailim bin Othman Al-Swailim, shortly after the province's establishment, this grand palace stands as a testament to the cultural richness of Najdi heritage.
The palace includes several facilities that highlight the architectural brilliance of the era.
Preserved with exceptional care, Maqsourat Al-Swailim maintains its beauty and historic integrity.
Asib Avenue offers a unique escape in the vibrant city of Buraydah, combining modern amenities with a touch of natural charm.
The avenue features a range of cafes, bakeries, and tea brands, along with exceptional restaurants serving diverse and delicious cuisines.
It’s also home to boutique shops perfect for shopping enthusiasts. For entertainment, visitors can enjoy an activity zone with games like archery and darts, providing fun for all ages.
Aseeb Avenue in Buraydah is the perfect spot for great food, exciting activities, and memorable moments with family and friends.
Jazan Province is known for its varied heritage. Near the southern corniche of Jazan City, a tourist attraction, established in 1439 Hijri, showcases the ancient history of the region.

It is a fine combination of archeological buildings, handicrafts, popular food restaurants, cultural programs, modern arts, and national festivals, which makes the Heritage Village of Jazan an engaging cultural landmark and tourist destination for all society groups

The historic Al Dosariyah Castle is located on a mountain overlooking the port of Jazan. It was built in 1933 for military purposes, and its elevated location provides a clear aerial view of the port and the horizon.

The castle was built with a military character and defensive systems such as protection walls installed at the entrances, an observation room on the upper floor, and openings in the walls for observation and shooting.
The Fifa Mountains, or as they are called "Neighbor of the Moon", are distinguished by their enchanting view, at an altitude of more than 1,800 km above sea level.
They are a series of mountains wrapped around one another, with peaks covered with green, including: Al-Lagha, Al-Kadrah, Baqat Al-Washl, Al-Surrah, Qardah, and Al-Sama'.
The highest one is Al-Absiyya summit. The Fifa Mountains are about 100 km from the city of Jazan, and the climate there is moderately characterized most of the year.
In winter, it tends to be cold in the high mountains, with a temperature of approximately 19-29 degrees Celsius.
Away from the hustle and bustle of the city, Jazan coast is a starting point for adventurous diving excursions and cruises, which promise you a great vacation.
Dream Divers is the way to have this fun, as it plans swimming and diving courses and excursions, under the supervision of diving experts and swimming coaches.
It also has a marketplace for diving and sailing equipment.
Muhammad ibn Abd Al-Wahhab Mosque is located in Al-Bujairi district in Diriyah, with a design that is consistent with the architectural style of the region.
It is surrounded by spaces decorated with green landscapes, palm trees, and stone terraces.
In the western side of Diriyah, Wadi Safar Dam is located on a 60-square meter area. It is an extension of Wadi Hanifa.

The location is characterized by its rural nature, and contains rock seating areas with wonderful views and a nice ambience, giving you the opportunity for a special picnic with family and friends in the weekend, surrounded by warm cups of tea, along with the aromas of barbecues.
Stunning mud-brick palaces, mosques, and homes make up this UNESCO World Heritage site. Today, the district has been carefully restored to its former glory.
Museums tell the story of the earliest settlers to this region, highlight the history of the Saudi state, and delve into the unique Najdi and Islamic architecture.
From the heart of Diriyah, with its rich history that accompanied the stages of founding and unifying the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, the Saudi flag rises on the flagpole of King Salman Square.
This flagpole is considered the tallest flagpole in the capital city of Riyadh.
Samhan Farm is 230 Kilometers away from Wadi Hanifah; it combines between the ancient past and modern present, it has beautiful green areas and lots of trees.
JAX District has successfully transformed the industrial heritage site in Diriyah, Saudi Arabia, into a vibrant hub for artists and creatives.

What was once known for its unique mud-brick architecture has now been reborn as the creative hub of the Saudi capital, beckoning talents to showcase their work amidst a supportive and thriving artistic community.

Al-Bujairi Heritage and Tourism Park is a lush oasis surrounded by palm trees, which includes great green landscapes, and natural landmarks such as plants, lakes, and heights, enabling you to enjoy moments of peace and tranquillity.
With a length of 120 km, Wadi Hanifa extends from the heights of Al-Haisiyah in the North to Al-Hayer in Southern Riyadh.
Within this vast area, you can make dozens of plans to enjoy the beauty of nature. Recreation facilities are available on both sides of the 57-km-long Wadi Hanifa water channel.

You are going to enjoy this trip to its fullest! Wadi Hanifa is uniquely redeveloped. Its banks are adorned with parks with complete facilities and services to allow visitors to enjoy the green landscapes in a joyful atmosphere in the open air.

Revive your energy with friends in the Mondial Courts in Diriyah and enjoy many games that come at the top of the list of the most important sports around the world, such as football, tennis, and many other sports.
You can enjoy these sports in 15 courts equipped with appropriate lighting and searchlights to continue playing any time throughout the week between 04:00 PM until 02:00 AM.

You will find many international and local restaurants and shops in Albujairi Terrace. On an area of ​​15,000 m2, Albujairi has intricate details inspired by the authenticity of Najd and its history full of amazing architecture, and has amazing views on the historical At-Turaif district, which is included in the UNESCO World Heritage List.
You can enjoy scenic natural views in a group picnic, or even alone in the designated bike lanes in the terrace.
Or you can walk in the paths that trace the Kingdom’s history and its stories when Diriyah was the capital of the first Saudi state.
In the calmness of nature away from the crowded city, you will find Sofie Farm, one of the best rural experiences that is available all week long, from 7:00 am to 7:00 pm.
Diriyah Terrace is an open space that includes several local and international restaurants and cafes and seating areas surrounded by tall palm trees.
The terrace is fragrant with the aroma of authentic Saudi coffee in a captivating night that gathers loved ones around a winter table in which American and Italian cuisines are present.
You can enjoy all of this with an open view of the sky, in the midst of bright golden lights and the melodies of music that fill the place.
In Diriyah Terrace, modern landmarks and historical glories embrace each other in one place.
Day or night, you can visit the Diriyah Walk to relieve the burdens of a long day, or to ignite your imagination with a flow of inspiring ideas.
Have a walk amid the cool breeze and the rustling of lush palm trees of Diriyah in safe and paved spaces.
Ghasiba district, located on the banks of Wadi Hanifa, is the core from which Diriyah was founded, and represents the beginning of its long history which exceeds 600 years.
With a storage capacity of 900 thousand m3 and a length of 170 meters, learn about the 50-year old Ghubaira Dam, one of the side dams of Wadi Hanifa in the new Diriyah.

Salwa Palace is a historical landmark that encapsulates a crucial time in the history of the Kingdom, for it stands as a window with a view that takes you back in time to the establishment of the First Saudi State.
It offers a chance to discover centuries-old architecture. It was given this name because its construction has multiple uses, making it a consolation for its residents and visitors.
Explore an 18th-century palace when you visit Diriyah Museum. Make your way through galleries to learn about the complete history of the region.
Discover the story of the House of Saud, the nation’s royal family, as well as the tribe that lived in the region before Diriyah was settled in 1446.
The palace itself is a stunning example of the region’s Najdi architecture.
Get a glimpse of what life was like for people living in the first Saudi state at this museum.
Housed in a historic palace, the Social Life Museum features recreations of guest rooms, servants' quarters, and meeting halls that were found in historic homes.
An audio guide walks visitors through each gallery, while artifacts on display include traditional clothing, furniture, tools, and cookware.
